build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 15: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 18's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 4-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 15's value table (side 3's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 15's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0030, channel 0's script at +$000E and 0 for channels 1, 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 11 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 5, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 2 then 8, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 12, frame 3 then 1, frame 1 then 1, frame 1 then 5, frame 4 then 15, frame 4 then 1. One pass takes 51 steps.

Picture 15's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $04 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 14 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 15, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 8 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 15, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 8 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 24 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 5 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 15, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 16 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 5 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 15, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 10 and 11: a run count of 0 to start, then 26 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 71 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 15's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,193rd byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
